theorem_reviews.argument: For unequal inputs, division by the nonzero input difference constructs the unique chord slope and cancellation reconstructs the output increment. For equal inputs, the output increment is exactly zero and the endpoint alpha is an admissible slope. Conversely an admissible chord slope cancels to the quotient for unequal inputs.
edge_cases: Negative input differences cause no inequality reversal: bounds are assumed on the quotient and only an equality is cancelled.
alpha = beta is supported; alpha > beta is excluded by the explicit hypothesis.
theorem_reviews.paper_correspondence: The website and arXiv v2 impose 0 <= alpha < beta < infinity. The ordered-real theorem covers that entire scope and additionally the degenerate interval; real parameters are finite.

The imported block-quadratic identity rewrites exactly to a weighted sum of coordinate scalar QCs. The quotient/chord equivalence supplies the actual chord hypothesis for each coordinate; nonnegative weights preserve the scalar inequalities.
edge_cases: Repeated coordinate inputs contribute zero scalar QCs.
The empty finite type has a zero quadratic form.
The multiplier is diagonal by construction, not an arbitrary PSD matrix.
theorem_reviews.paper_correspondence: Together with diagonal_qc_matrix_is_stated_block, this is precisely arXiv v2 Lemma 1 equation (9), with T = diagonal(multiplier).

theorem_reviews.argument: The all-multipliers equivalence isolates the only coordinate. scalar_qc_iff_admissible_chord recovers an admissible chord, and quotient_definition_iff_all_chords yields every unequal-input quotient bound. The hypothesis uses diagonalQC rather than the block form; diagonal_qc_is_actual_block_quadratic proves those expressions are equal.
edge_cases: The use of Fin 1 avoids a vacuous empty-coordinate converse.
Equal inputs recover a zero chord; the conclusion quantifies only unequal inputs.
Nonnegative weights include the unit coordinate selector.
theorem_reviews.paper_correspondence: This is a derived converse supporting the exact definition correspondence. It is not attributed as an additional theorem of Fazlyab et al.

edge_cases: Negative weights still give the algebraic diagonal identity.
The empty sum is the zero diagonal matrix.

edge_cases: The theorem says nothing about admissibility of a general non-diagonal PSD multiplier.
